title: Demo talk track (rough draft) — v0.6 (timed + branching)
content:
NOTE: This is the *spoken* version. Deck outline is separate. This draft is meant to be usable by AEs/SEs with minimal improv, but still flexible.

House rules
- Ask 2–3 discovery questions early, then pick a branch (Hosted-first vs Dedicated-first vs Private/security-first)
- Avoid deep kernel/runtime internals unless they ask (save for Q&A)
- Always have a “backup mode” path: screenshots + canned outputs if live steps fail
- Keep it to 25–30 min default. Exec version is 15–20 min.

Legend
- [T+mm:ss] timing
- (AE) vs (SE) speaker
- {branch: Hosted | Dedicated | Private} optional modules
- [CLICK] console actions
- [RUN] terminal/app actions
- [SS#] placeholder screenshot/slide

========================
0) Pre-flight (not on the call)
========================
Owner: SE
- Confirm demo tenant healthcheck is green (quota, model pins, ingestion) — see runbook
- Open tabs: Console (Projects, Routes, Observability), Demo app, terminal for curl, (optional) Grafana-like dashboard if relevant
- Have backup screenshots ready: rollouts view, audit log view, VPC architecture diagram

Quick checklist:
- API key works (scoped demo key)
- Synthetic traffic generator ran within last 30–60 min (dashboards not empty)
- Demo routes pinned to known-good model versions

========================
1) Opening + discovery
========================
[T+00:00–01:30] (AE)
“Thanks for the time. The goal today is to show how Redwood makes LLM inference predictable in production — cost, latency, reliability — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We’ll do a quick live flow, then show what it looks like to operate it day-to-day.”

[T+01:30–03:30] (AE) discovery questions (pick 2–3)
1) “What’s the user-facing feature? Chat assistant, search, support, internal tooling?”
2) “What matters more right now: latency, cost, or reliability under spikes?”
3) “Where do you need to run inference: public cloud, VPC, on-prem, multiple regions?”
4) “Do you have constraints like SSO, audit logs, retention, residency?”

Decision note (internal):
- If they say: “we just want to ship fast” → Hosted branch
- If they say: “noisy neighbor / throughput predictability / SLA” → Dedicated branch
- If they say: “regulated / VPC / audit” → Private branch (narrative + screenshots)

[T+03:30–04:00] (AE) agenda framing
“I’ll show three things: (1) the API experience, (2) how we control production economics, and (3) reliability + observability so this doesn’t become a science project.”

========================
2) Core API demo: streaming + structured output + tool calling
========================
[T+04:00–04:30] (SE)
“I’ll start with the developer surface area. Same API whether you’re hosted, dedicated, or private.”

[T+04:30–07:30] (SE) Live step: chat completion w/ streaming
[RUN] demo app “Support Agent” or “Travel planner” scenario
- Show tokens streaming
- Point out: latency is dominated by first-token; streaming improves perceived latency

Script line:
“Most teams start here: a simple chat completion. Redwood is optimized for steady first-token and stable throughput under load.”

If they ask “which model is this?”
- Answer: “We pin a model/version per route. You can swap models without rewriting app code.”

[T+07:30–09:30] (SE) Live step: structured output
[RUN] same app / endpoint, request JSON schema output (e.g., {"action":"refund|replace|escalate","confidence":0–1,"reason":string})

Script line:
“Structured outputs reduce downstream parsing and failure modes — especially when this output feeds workflows.”

[T+09:30–11:30] (SE) Live step: tool calling
[RUN] tool/function call that hits a stub “Order status” tool
- show tool call + tool result + final response

Script line:
“This is where reliability matters: your app is now a chain of calls. We focus on predictable latency and error handling so these flows don’t fall over.”

Backup mode (if tool calling flakes):
- [SS1] “tool-calling transcript screenshot”
- Use canned output from doc: TODO add

========================
3) Production economics: cost/latency levers (batching/caching) + token breakdown
========================
[T+11:30–12:00] (AE) transition
“Where teams get stuck isn’t getting a response — it’s unit economics at scale. Let’s show what levers you can pull, and that it’s observable.”

[T+12:00–15:30] (SE) Console: token-level breakdown
[CLICK] Console → Observability → Costs/Latency
- show per-route view: tokens, latency p50/p95, error rate
- show a request trace (if stable)

Script line:
“You can see cost and latency by route/model, not just at the account level. This is the difference between ‘we think it’s expensive’ and ‘we know exactly which endpoint and which prompt is expensive.’”

[T+15:30–17:30] (SE) Toggle economics controls
Option A (preferred): show route config toggles (batching/caching)
[CLICK] Console → Routes → ‘demo-chat’ → Performance
- toggle/point at: batching policy, caching, max concurrency
- explain tradeoffs

Option B (if UI not stable): talk + screenshot
- [SS2] route performance controls screenshot

Script line:
“Redwood gives you controlled, measurable knobs: batching and caching to lower cost per token, without guessing. We don’t ask you to rebuild infra to try these.”

Prompt for customer:
“Do you have workload patterns like repeated prefixes (agents), repeated templates (support), or bursts (product launches)?”

If they press on “what’s the % savings?”
- Say: “It depends on sequence lengths and repetition. In practice we see meaningful improvements when there’s shared prefixes or stable templates. We’ll quantify it in a POC with your prompts.”

========================
4) Reliability demo: fallback routing + graceful degradation
========================
[T+17:30–18:00] (AE) setup
“Let’s talk about what happens when the real world happens: model rollout changes, region issues, or sudden spikes.”

[T+18:00–21:00] (SE) Live (preferred): induce a controlled failure + show fallback
[RUN] hit route configured with ‘primary model’ + allowed fallback variant
- step 1: show normal response
- step 2: simulate capacity constraint or disable primary (demo toggle)
- step 3: show request still succeeds, with banner/log that fallback occurred

Script line:
“Instead of an outage, you get graceful degradation: compatible model variant or region with policy controls. You choose the rules.”

If live failure injection is too risky today:
- [SS3] rollout/fallback view screenshot
- [SS4] trace showing fallback decision

Important phrasing:
“We’re not hiding failures. We make them survivable and observable.”

Common question: “Will fallback change output quality?”
- Answer: “Potentially, yes — which is why fallback is constrained by family/compatibility, and we recommend eval gates. The point is to keep the app online while you recover.”

========================
5) Observability + operations: rollouts, canary/A-B, errors
========================
[T+21:00–23:30] (SE)
[CLICK] Console → Rollouts (or Deployments)
- show model version pin
- show staged rollout (canary)
- point to error analysis

Script line:
“Serving is a product surface: versioning, safe rollouts, and fast debugging. We treat inference like any other production service.”

If dashboards are empty (known demo failure mode):
- Don’t panic. Say:
“Everything you’re seeing is synthetic demo traffic; the demo environment can occasionally get ‘quiet.’ We’ll switch to backup screenshots while we re-run the traffic generator.”
- [SS5] full dashboard screenshot
- SE runs traffic job off-screen if feasible

========================
6) Branch modules by customer type
========================

A) {branch: Hosted-first} (2–3 min)
[T+23:30–26:00] (AE)
“For teams starting with hosted, the key is: fast integration + production-grade reliability without picking infrastructure up front.”

Show:
- API keys + rate limits (brief)
- multi-region routing (brief)
- “same API later on Dedicated/Private” line

Ask:
“Is your first milestone shipping a v1 feature, or do you already have scale constraints?”


B) {branch: Dedicated-first} (3–5 min)
[T+23:30–28:00] (AE/SE)
Use when they say: unpredictable throughput, noisy neighbors, guaranteed capacity, SLAs.

Script:
“Dedicated is for predictable throughput and data isolation. You get reserved capacity with policies that mirror production, but without building your own serving layer.”

Show (live if possible):
- [CLICK] Project → Quotas / Capacity (Dedicated-style controls)
- [SS6] capacity/reserved pool diagram

Key bullets to hit:
- isolation (no noisy neighbor)
- predictable throughput / latency SLO targets
- scaling policies + burst handling

Procurement-friendly line:
“This becomes a capacity commitment with clear sizing and SLAs.”


C) {branch: Private/security-first} (5–7 min, mostly narrative)
[T+23:30–30:00] (AE/SE)
Use when security reviewer present.

Script:
“Private deployments are about running Redwood’s control plane in your environment — VPC and on-prem options — with enterprise controls: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, retention.”

Show:
- [SS7] VPC/Private architecture diagram
- [SS8] SSO/SAML + RBAC screenshot
- [SS9] audit log screenshot (safe, synthetic)

Be careful:
- Do not imply customer data in the demo environment
- Emphasize synthetic dataset + least-privilege keys

Answer short:
- Data retention: “Configurable retention controls + audit logs; details in security FAQ.”
- Residency: “Region pinning + private deployment options.”

========================
7) Close + next steps
========================
[T+30:00–32:00] (AE)
“Let’s align on what ‘success’ looks like for you. Typically we do a short POC where we:
1) port 1–2 endpoints,
2) run your prompt set / evals,
3) measure latency/cost, and
4) validate reliability behaviors (fallback/rollouts).”

Ask:
- “Who else needs to weigh in — platform, security, procurement?”
- “What’s the timeline and decision path?”

CTA options:
- POC proposal meeting (45 min)
- Security review call
- Dedicated sizing session

========================
Appendix: micro-scripts for objections (rough)
========================

Objection: “We can just run vLLM ourselves.”
Response:
“You can, and many teams start there. The hard part is everything around it: reliability under spikes, rollouts, observability, routing/fallback, and doing it across environments. Redwood is the productized layer that keeps unit economics and SLOs predictable.”

Objection: “How do we avoid vendor lock-in?”
Response:
“We focus on open model ecosystems and consistent interfaces. You can pin versions, swap models per route, and choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployment — without rewriting app integration.”

Objection: “Fallback sounds risky.”
Response:
“It’s policy-based and constrained. The alternative is downtime. We make it survivable and visible, and we pair it with eval gates so you know what you’re trading.”

========================
TODOs / placeholders
========================
- Add exact demo app scenario names + commands (Alex/Renee)
- Insert real screenshot references once Design delivers annotated set (DES-611)
  - [SS1] tool calling transcript
  - [SS2] route performance controls
  - [SS3] fallback routing view
  - [SS5] populated dashboards (golden)
  - [SS7] private/VPC architecture
  - [SS9] audit logs (synthetic)
- Confirm which Console views are stable enough to demo week-to-week (Dylan/Chloe)
- Tighten wording around “Optimize” naming (field feedback: some customers think it’s a separate product)

Change log (rough)
- v0.4 (2025-11-06): added reliability + fallback module after internal runthrough feedback (customers asked earlier)
- v0.5 (2025-11-10): added Private/security narrative branch + safe-sharing warnings
